caption:
Everything that happened in the shipping industry in the last 24 hours (18 Nov 2026) 🚢

1. Brent slips to $92.6 on US stock build
2. ADNOC ship hit in Hormuz - 1 missing, 11 injured
3. Tara Gas abandoned on fire - Indian seafarer missing
4. Two ships lost off Bulgaria - 31 crew rescued
5. Armed skiff tries boarding - guards fire warning shot
6. Filipino steward wins $95,000 disability case
7. Knutsen delivers last QatarEnergy LNG carrier
8. ONE returns to Suez Canal after three years
9. CIMC SOE wins 10 MR tankers order

Sources are credited on each slide. Follow @jaimarineshorts for daily shipping news.

stories.headline: Brent slips to [$92.6] on US stock build
stories.summary: Brent crude fell about 0.5% to around $92.6 a barrel on Wednesday, 18 Nov, while US WTI dropped 1.15% to near $85. API data showed US crude stocks rose 5.28 million barrels last week. Losses were limited by continuing US-Iran hostilities and tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: ADNOC ship hit in Hormuz - [1 missing, 11 injured]
stories.summary: A vessel of UAE company ADNOC Logistics & Services was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on the evening of 17 Nov. One crew member is missing and 11 are injured and receiving medical care. All other crew were evacuated. Search and rescue continues. The ship's name and the attacker were not given.
stories.photo_credit: Representative · Michael Martin from Cypress, Texas / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

stories.headline: Tara Gas abandoned on fire - [Indian seafarer missing]
stories.summary: The Panama-flagged LPG carrier Tara Gas was hit by a drone on 16 Nov about 7 nm north of Khasab, Oman, and struck again on 17 Nov. The crew abandoned the burning ship. A salvage company rescued 24 Indian crew; two are in hospital and one Indian seafarer is missing. India called the attacks deeply worrisome.

stories.headline: Two ships lost off Bulgaria - [31 crew rescued]
stories.summary: Black Sea attacks hit two more ships in Bulgaria's waters. On 16 Nov the cargo ship Betul 8 capsized off Cape Kaliakra; all 12 crew were airlifted. On 17 Nov the Liberia-flagged LPG carrier Gas Husky, managed by Stealth Maritime, was struck; all 19 Filipino crew were rescued, two with minor injuries. Drone attacks are suspected, not officially confirmed.

stories.headline: Armed skiff tries boarding - [guards fire warning shot]
stories.summary: A cargo ship about 50 nm southwest of Al Mukalla, Yemen, reported on 17 Nov that a skiff carrying weapons and ladders tried to board it in the Gulf of Aden. The ship's armed security team fired a warning shot. The skiff turned away and returned to its mothership. No injuries were reported.

stories.headline: Filipino steward wins [$95,000] disability case
stories.summary: The Philippine Supreme Court ordered RCCL Crew Management and Royal Caribbean to pay galley steward Jonathan Ian Ponio $95,000. He developed an ear infection on board that left permanent hearing loss. The court said employers must give a written final medical assessment within 120 or 240 days, or the disability becomes total and permanent.
stories.photo_credit: Representative · Matthew T Rader / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

stories.headline: Knutsen delivers [last QatarEnergy] LNG carrier
stories.summary: Knutsen has taken delivery of the 174,000 cbm LNG carrier Hazem Baranyoush, built by HD Hyundai under a 2022 order. It is the tenth and final ship in Knutsen's series for QatarEnergy and its 27th vessel under the French flag. The ship is chartered to QatarEnergy.
stories.photo_credit: Representative · 青空白帆 / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.1 jp)

stories.headline: ONE returns to [Suez Canal] after three years
stories.summary: Ocean Network Express made its first Suez Canal transit in nearly three years when the 8,110 TEU ONE Continuity sailed north on 15 Nov from Singapore toward the Netherlands. Maersk, Hapag-Lloyd, Evergreen and Premier Alliance lines are also switching routes back. Drewry counted 53 container ships through the canal in early November.

stories.headline: CIMC SOE wins [10 MR tankers] order
stories.summary: China's CIMC SOE signed contracts with Singapore's Stamford Shipping for ten 49,900 dwt MR product tankers, the yard's first MR order and the owner's first newbuild deal. A European owner ordered two more of the same design. Delivery is due in 2029-2030. About 190 MR2 tankers have been ordered this year.
stories.photo_credit: Representative · Niels Johannes / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
